_meta.system: C3 photosynthesis (Spinacia oleracea / Arabidopsis thaliana reference)
sources: Cramer et al. 2011 Biochim Biophys Acta
Stitt et al. 2010 Plant Cell Environ
_meta.note: N-D-C values derived from published quantum yields, rate constants, and stoichiometries. Balance scores reflect transparency tier midpoints adjusted for known constraints.

synthetic.label: C3 Canonical Baseline
synthetic.description: Spinacia oleracea / Arabidopsis thaliana reference values at 25°C, 380 ppm CO2, saturating light, unstressed conditions.

0.name: Light Harvesting
0.transformation: Photon absorption and excitation energy transfer

7.name: Carbon Export
7.transformation: Triose phosphate export; sucrose and starch synthesis

0.notes: Incident photons -> excitation energy at reaction center. High D from spectral and structural constraints; high C from near-perfect energy transfer efficiency.
0.key_metric: Leaf absorptance PAR = 0.85; LHCII energy transfer efficiency >0.95
0.stress_mode: NPQ activation under excess light; Fv/Fm depression under chronic stress

1.notes: Excitation at P680 -> O2 evolution and plastoquinol. D reflects strict electrochemical and structural requirements of the Mn4CaO5 cluster.
1.key_metric: Fv/Fm = 0.83 (dark-adapted); O2 evolution ~28 µmol m-2 s-1 at saturation
1.stress_mode: Photoinhibition: D1 protein oxidative damage reduces Fv/Fm; Mn cluster disruption under Mn deficiency

2.notes: PQH2 -> reduced plastocyanin + proton gradient. Near-perfect D-C balance; cytochrome b6f is rate-limiting but well-matched to upstream supply.
2.key_metric: Cytochrome b6f turnover ~150 e- complex-1 s-1; pmf ~175 mV steady-state
2.stress_mode: Cold temperature reduces cytochrome b6f rate; state transitions limit linear flow under fluctuating light

3.notes: Reduced plastocyanin -> NADPH via ferredoxin. Slight C advantage reflects multiple downstream outputs (NADPH, cyclic flow, N/S assimilation).
3.key_metric: PSI quantum yield Y(I) ~0.80; NADPH production ~10 µmol m-2 s-1
3.stress_mode: Acceptor-side limitation when NADP+ depleted under drought; PSI photoinhibition under fluctuating light

4.notes: pmf -> ATP. Near-perfect balance. H+/ATP = 4.67 in spinach; ATP deficit relative to Calvin cycle demand is met by cyclic electron flow.
4.key_metric: H+/ATP = 4.67 (14/3); ATP/NADPH ratio from linear flow = 1.28 (demand = 1.5)
4.stress_mode: Drought or salt stress destabilizes pmf via passive H+ leak; reduces ATP synthesis efficiency

5.notes: CO2 fixation by Rubisco. Significant D-C imbalance: high D from O2 competition and CO2 substrate limitation (Rubisco operates near its Km). Photorespiration wastes ~25% of light energy.
5.key_metric: An = 20 µmol CO2 m-2 s-1; Vo/Vc = 0.25 at 25°C; Rubisco Sc/o = 80
5.stress_mode: Photorespiration: amplified by high temperature (Sc/o decreases) and drought (stomatal closure raises O2/CO2 ratio inside leaf). Primary ecological bottleneck of C3 photosynthesis.

6.notes: 3-PGA -> G3P; RuBP regeneration. Well-balanced phase. ATP and NADPH stoichiometry tightly matched to demand when phase 5 and 4 are functioning normally.
6.key_metric: Stoichiometry: 3 ATP + 2 NADPH per CO2; G3P export ~4 µmol triose-P m-2 s-1
6.stress_mode: TPU (triose phosphate utilization) limitation under high CO2 or cold: G3P accumulates and backs up Calvin cycle

7.notes: G3P -> sucrose/starch; phloem loading. Slight D excess reflects regulatory complexity of source-sink coupling. Export efficiency ~75% of fixed carbon.
7.key_metric: Sucrose synthesis ~12 µmol C m-2 s-1; starch ~6 µmol C m-2 s-1; export fraction ~0.65
7.stress_mode: Sink limitation: low sink demand (cold, nutrient stress) causes sucrose feedback, starch accumulation, and indirect reduction of An

synthetic.interpretation: The C3 photosynthesis energy chain is highly coherent in its light reaction phases (0-4) but faces a structural bottleneck at Phase 5 (Rubisco carbon fixation) due to photorespiration. The D-C imbalance at Phase 5 reflects the evolutionary constraint of Rubisco operating simultaneously as a carboxylase and oxygenase under present atmospheric conditions.
